originalTitle: US stocks: S&P closes at record high as soft jobs report eases rate-hike concerns
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a great day on Friday, with the S&P (a measure of the stock market) reaching its highest point ever. This happened because there were more job losses than expected, which made people think that interest rates might not go up as soon as thought. When interest rates are low, it's often good for the stock market, which is why the market went up. Additionally, some big companies had strong earnings, which also helped the market, and lower oil prices made people less worried about inflation. This all combined to make it a good day for the stock market.

originalTitle: Market cuts odds of Fed hike after jobs data, but economists still see case for tightening
simplifiedContent: Recently, the number of new jobs created in July was lower than expected, which has made people less sure that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates soon. Because of this, the market is now less likely to expect an interest rate increase next month. Some Federal Reserve officials think rates should be increased to control inflation, but not everyone agrees. The Federal Reserve is paying close attention to inflation to help make decisions about interest rates. This matters because changes to interest rates can affect the overall economy and the stock market.

originalTitle: Dollar falls against yen, euro as weak US jobs data clouds Fed outlook
simplifiedContent: The value of the US dollar went down compared to the yen and euro on Friday. This happened because the US recently announced that it lost jobs in July, which was not expected and is causing people to worry about the economy. Even though the percentage of people without jobs (called the unemployment rate) actually went down, another important measure (labor force participation) hit a very low level that it hasn't seen in a long time. This news is making it unclear what the Federal Reserve (the US central bank) will do with interest rates, which is important for the economy and the stock market. As a result, investors are selling US dollars, which is why its value is going down.

originalTitle: Short-Term Treasuries Cap Biggest Weekly Rally Since May on Data
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: the US government's short-term borrowing costs (called Treasuries) had a big increase in value this week, which is the largest gain since May. This happened because a recent report on jobs in the US was weaker than expected. As a result, investors think the Federal Reserve (the country's central bank) might not raise interest rates as much as they thought. This matters because when interest rates are lower, it can affect the overall economy and stock market. The increase in value of these short-term Treasuries is a sign that investors are adjusting their expectations about what the Federal Reserve will do next.

originalTitle: Treasury yields fall as jobs report dashes hike bets
simplifiedContent: The US government releases a report on jobs, which showed that the job market is not as strong as people thought. Because of this, people are now guessing that interest rates might not go up as much as they thought. This caused the "yields" on government bonds (called Treasuries) to go down. Yields are like the return on investment for these bonds, so when they go down, it means the bonds are becoming more attractive to buy. This change in yields matters because it can affect the overall direction of the stock market and the economy.

originalTitle: Gold hits seven-week high as weak US jobs data dents rate hike bets
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has reached its highest point in seven weeks. This happened because the latest jobs data from the US was weaker than expected, which made investors think that interest rates might not be increased as quickly as they thought. As a result, people are buying more gold, which is why its price is going up. This change in gold's price matters because it can affect the overall direction of the stock market and investing decisions. The weaker jobs data and higher gold price may indicate that the economy is not as strong as thought, which can impact investments.
